claims.text: A concession first, so the record is not overstated on the rider's side: the trace-measured excess on this trip is 1.33 km, which is 6.72% of the 19.8 km optimal route. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to pass BOTH gates - greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km - and the percentage limb fails, so no route deviation is established and no distance-or-time refund under POL-RD-02 is available on this trip. The rider does not contest the 1.33 km of extra driving. The amount contested is S$4.00, and that figure is exactly the ERP line, which is what this dispute is actually about.

The toll the rider is charged for is a gantry the platform's own optimal route does not use. The booking-time optimal route - routing-engine-v3.2, PIE then Nicoll Hwy - carries optimal_route_erp_sgd of 0.0, and the fare ledger's single ERP line, S$4.00 at 'ECP (Fort Rd towards City)', is flagged on_optimal_route: false. So the entire S$4.00 contested is a pass-through charge that only exists because the vehicle was driven on a corridor the optimal route avoids.

That S$4.00 has been paid twice for one crossing, and the driver does not deny it. The rider's account is that the driver asked for cash at the gantry and he paid it; the driver's own counterparty statement confirms the cash collection ('I told him about the cash because sometimes the app doesn't capture it') and adds 'If the app also charged, refund him the app one.' The ledger shows the app did capture it: tolls_erp 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0. POL-RD-09 requires third-party and government-set pass-through charges to be settled separately from distance and time and never to be counted twice; a gantry that has been paid in cash and billed again in the app has been counted twice, and the duplicate in-app line should be refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction. The same result follows on POL-RD-09(4)'s footing, in the alternative: a charge line the rider did not owe is a billing-integrity defect refundable in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and here the rider owed this S$4.00 once, not twice.

The rider does not put this as a phantom gantry, and the trace shows why he should not: the driver's own trace has a fix at 2026-09-11T15:43:10+08:00 at 0.0 m from the ECP (Fort Rd towards City) gantry, the same timestamp as charged_at on the fare ledger, so the vehicle genuinely crossed it once. What the trace and the ledger together establish is one crossing charged twice - once in cash at the gantry on the driver's request, once again on the app ledger. The defect is duplication, not a gantry that was never crossed, and the correction is the removal of the duplicated line.

The driver's justification - that ECP 'is the normal airport route' and that he had discretion - is backed by no artifact on this record. Any traffic-based justification for leaving the optimal corridor would have to be tested under POL-RD-03 against a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route uses; the bundle's only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00523-01, is MISSING - status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, no payload - so no advisory covers this trip's corridor or window and the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run on the record. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion therefore carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and the driver's statement cites no evidence ID of its own. The rider cites the absence itself, and discloses that the artifact is weight 0.0 and carries no fact; every artifact the rider relies on for the money - the fare ledger, the trip record and the trace - is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The whole contested amount is the duplicated toll and nothing else, so returning the S$4.00 makes the rider whole on the entire dispute and the outcome is the full contested amount rather than a fraction of it. The platform's answer that the driver 'has discretion on routes' answers a route-length complaint the rider is not pressing; it does not answer the double charge, and it is no answer to POL-RD-09's rule that a pass-through cost is never counted twice.

The ruling distance is the GPS trace, not the trip record's rounded convenience copy. EV-GPS-00523 records trace_distance_km of 21.13 km against the booked optimal of 19.8 km, an excess of 1.33 km — 6.72% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km absolute; 6.72% fails the percentage limb outright, so no route deviation exists on this trip and the enquiry ends at POL-RD-01.

Both POL-RD-01 gates must pass and only one does. The 1.33 km excess clears the 0.8 km absolute limb, but the percentage limb fails, and POL-RD-01 makes the consequences of a single failed limb explicit: 'no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip'. The qualifying percentage is read from the unimpaired trace, not from the trip record's rounded deviation_pct of 6.6.

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is never discharged and therefore never shifts to the driver. The rider must first show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold; the only excess the trace yields is 6.72%, below 20%. With no threshold-qualifying excess the burden does not move, and the driver need not invoke any exculpatory clause at all — his ECP route choice is never reached on the merits.

The chat log for this trip is empty — zero messages, null first and last message timestamps, truncated false (EV-CHAT-00523). Neither the rider's account of agreeing to the expressway nor the driver's account of flagging the ERP charge is corroborated by a single message, and POL-RD-08 provides that assertions citing no evidence ID carry no weight. This case is decided on the telemetry, and the telemetry records no deviation.

The SGD 4.00 ERP line is a genuine pass-through, not a phantom charge. The trace passes the ECP (Fort Rd towards City) gantry at a nearest-fix distance of 0.0 m on the fix timestamped 15:43:10, precisely the timestamp the ledger charges. POL-RD-09(4)'s billing-integrity limb bites only on a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes, and this gantry is crossed on the trace itself.

No standalone ERP correction is available on these facts. POL-RD-09 provides a pass-through refund only inside a POL-RD-02 deviation refund (limb 1), on a POL-RD-03 closure exoneration (limb 2), or for a phantom gantry (limb 4). There is no established deviation, the one advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT so it carries no fact of any kind, and the gantry was in fact crossed. POL-RD-13 confirms the absent advisory supplies neither an amended optimal nor an excuse.

The SGD 6.00 airport surcharge is properly chargeable and is not a billing defect. POL-RD-09(4) makes a surcharge a billing-integrity failure only on a trip that does not ORIGINATE at an airport, and this trip ORIGINATED at Changi Airport Terminal 3, Departure Level Door 5.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be established against this driver under POL-RD-06. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, below the 3-flag gate, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 is 0, below the 0.05 ratio. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follow. POL-RD-06 is in any event consulted only on a MATERIAL deviation, and a 6.72% excess is neither material nor even established.

NO_ACTION is the outcome the record supports, and it is party-relative and therefore a driver win here. The dispute is rider-filed and the ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so NO_ACTION leaves the fare standing and confirms it to the driver; it does not restore, reverse or re-open anything.

The rider's central complaint — that the toll was paid twice — is not evidenced on this record. The fare_breakdown carries exactly one ERP line, SGD 4.00 for the gantry the trace actually crossed, and the bundle holds no receipt, no second ledger line and no chat message recording any cash payment. There is no duplicate charge for the tribunal to reverse and no billing-integrity finding available under POL-RD-09.

To the rider and the driver — two questions are in this case and they come out differently.

1) The route itself was not a refundable deviation. Both sides agree on the arithmetic: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00523, trace_distance_km 21.13) against the booked optimal of 19.8 km (EV-TRIP-00523) is an excess of 1.33 km, or 6.72%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess passes BOTH gates — more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km. The percentage limb fails, so no deviation exists and no distance-or-time refund is available under POL-RD-02. The driver's explanation that ECP 'is the normal airport route' is a traffic assertion backed by no artifact; the only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00523-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 it carries no weight — but the result does not depend on it, because the deviation fails on the numbers alone. The rider's complaint that he was taken 'on a route I didn't choose' is therefore not made out.

2) The S$4.00 actually in dispute is refunded. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-00523) carries one ERP line, S$4.00 at ECP (Fort Rd towards City), and the trace shows the vehicle did cross that gantry once (a fix at 0.0 m at 15:43:10, the ledger's charged_at). But the driver's own statement records that he asked for and took that toll in cash at the gantry and adds: 'If the app also charged, refund him the app one.' The ledger shows the app did charge it — tolls_erp 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. One crossing was collected twice, and POL-RD-09 requires a third-party/government pass-through charge never to be counted twice. The duplicate S$4.00 is returned to the rider. I reject the driver's claim that no duplicate is evidenced: it is evidenced by the driver's own admission together with the ledger. I do not rest this on POL-RD-09(4): the gantry was in fact crossed and the S$6.00 airport surcharge is properly chargeable because the trip ORIGINATED at Changi Terminal 3, so no billing-integrity referral fires and none is added.

Other points. The chat log for the trip (EV-CHAT-00523) is empty — zero messages — so neither party's narrative is corroborated by a message; the driver's statement is used only as a concession, which is evidence in its own right. No repeat-deviation pattern can be found (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 250 completed trips), so there is no POL-RD-06 uplift and no driver-conduct referral. Because the route complaint fails while the toll claim succeeds, the outcome is a partial refund, even though the whole contested S$4.00 is returned.

Money lines (read off the fare breakdown): charged_total S$38.83; the disputed and refunded line is the S$4.00 ERP; recomputed distance/time is not run because no deviation exists. Amount payable to the rider: S$4.00.

The absolute gate passes; the percentage gate fails, and one failed gate means no deviation exists. No distance-or-time refund under POL-RD-02 is available, and both sides accept this. The driver's route choice on length therefore stands unmodified.

ledger.claim: A concession first, so the record is not overstated on the rider's side: the trace-measured excess on this trip is 1.33 km, which is 6.72% of the 19.8 km optimal route. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to pass BOTH gates - greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km - and the percentage limb fails, so no route deviation is established and no distance-or-time refund under POL-RD-02 is available on this trip. The rider does not contest the 1.33 km of extra driving. The amount contested is S$4.00, and that figure is exactly the ERP line, which is what this dispute is actually about.

The toll the rider is charged for is a gantry the platform's own optimal route does not use. The booking-time optimal route - routing-engine-v3.2, PIE then Nicoll Hwy - carries optimal_route_erp_sgd of 0.0, and the fare ledger's single ERP line, S$4.00 at 'ECP (Fort Rd towards City)', is flagged on_optimal_route: false. So the entire S$4.00 contested is a pass-through charge that only exists because the vehicle was driven on a corridor the optimal route avoids.

That S$4.00 has been paid twice for one crossing, and the driver does not deny it. The rider's account is that the driver asked for cash at the gantry and he paid it; the driver's own counterparty statement confirms the cash collection ('I told him about the cash because sometimes the app doesn't capture it') and adds 'If the app also charged, refund him the app one.' The ledger shows the app did capture it: tolls_erp 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0. POL-RD-09 requires third-party and government-set pass-through charges to be settled separately from distance and time and never to be counted twice; a gantry that has been paid in cash and billed again in the app has been counted twice, and the duplicate in-app line should be refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction. The same result follows on POL-RD-09(4)'s footing, in the alternative: a charge line the rider did not owe is a billing-integrity defect refundable in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and here the rider owed this S$4.00 once, not twice.

The rider does not put this as a phantom gantry, and the trace shows why he should not: the driver's own trace has a fix at 2026-09-11T15:43:10+08:00 at 0.0 m from the ECP (Fort Rd towards City) gantry, the same timestamp as charged_at on the fare ledger, so the vehicle genuinely crossed it once. What the trace and the ledger together establish is one crossing charged twice - once in cash at the gantry on the driver's request, once again on the app ledger. The defect is duplication, not a gantry that was never crossed, and the correction is the removal of the duplicated line.

The driver's justification - that ECP 'is the normal airport route' and that he had discretion - is backed by no artifact on this record. Any traffic-based justification for leaving the optimal corridor would have to be tested under POL-RD-03 against a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route uses; the bundle's only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00523-01, is MISSING - status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, no payload - so no advisory covers this trip's corridor or window and the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run on the record. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion therefore carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and the driver's statement cites no evidence ID of its own. The rider cites the absence itself, and discloses that the artifact is weight 0.0 and carries no fact; every artifact the rider relies on for the money - the fare ledger, the trip record and the trace - is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The whole contested amount is the duplicated toll and nothing else, so returning the S$4.00 makes the rider whole on the entire dispute and the outcome is the full contested amount rather than a fraction of it. The platform's answer that the driver 'has discretion on routes' answers a route-length complaint the rider is not pressing; it does not answer the double charge, and it is no answer to POL-RD-09's rule that a pass-through cost is never counted twice.

The ruling distance is the GPS trace, not the trip record's rounded convenience copy. EV-GPS-00523 records trace_distance_km of 21.13 km against the booked optimal of 19.8 km, an excess of 1.33 km — 6.72% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km absolute; 6.72% fails the percentage limb outright, so no route deviation exists on this trip and the enquiry ends at POL-RD-01.

Both POL-RD-01 gates must pass and only one does. The 1.33 km excess clears the 0.8 km absolute limb, but the percentage limb fails, and POL-RD-01 makes the consequences of a single failed limb explicit: 'no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip'. The qualifying percentage is read from the unimpaired trace, not from the trip record's rounded deviation_pct of 6.6.

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is never discharged and therefore never shifts to the driver. The rider must first show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold; the only excess the trace yields is 6.72%, below 20%. With no threshold-qualifying excess the burden does not move, and the driver need not invoke any exculpatory clause at all — his ECP route choice is never reached on the merits.

The chat log for this trip is empty — zero messages, null first and last message timestamps, truncated false (EV-CHAT-00523). Neither the rider's account of agreeing to the expressway nor the driver's account of flagging the ERP charge is corroborated by a single message, and POL-RD-08 provides that assertions citing no evidence ID carry no weight. This case is decided on the telemetry, and the telemetry records no deviation.

The SGD 4.00 ERP line is a genuine pass-through, not a phantom charge. The trace passes the ECP (Fort Rd towards City) gantry at a nearest-fix distance of 0.0 m on the fix timestamped 15:43:10, precisely the timestamp the ledger charges. POL-RD-09(4)'s billing-integrity limb bites only on a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes, and this gantry is crossed on the trace itself.

No standalone ERP correction is available on these facts. POL-RD-09 provides a pass-through refund only inside a POL-RD-02 deviation refund (limb 1), on a POL-RD-03 closure exoneration (limb 2), or for a phantom gantry (limb 4). There is no established deviation, the one advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT so it carries no fact of any kind, and the gantry was in fact crossed. POL-RD-13 confirms the absent advisory supplies neither an amended optimal nor an excuse.

The SGD 6.00 airport surcharge is properly chargeable and is not a billing defect. POL-RD-09(4) makes a surcharge a billing-integrity failure only on a trip that does not ORIGINATE at an airport, and this trip ORIGINATED at Changi Airport Terminal 3, Departure Level Door 5.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be established against this driver under POL-RD-06. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, below the 3-flag gate, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 is 0, below the 0.05 ratio. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follow. POL-RD-06 is in any event consulted only on a MATERIAL deviation, and a 6.72% excess is neither material nor even established.

NO_ACTION is the outcome the record supports, and it is party-relative and therefore a driver win here. The dispute is rider-filed and the ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so NO_ACTION leaves the fare standing and confirms it to the driver; it does not restore, reverse or re-open anything.

The rider's central complaint — that the toll was paid twice — is not evidenced on this record. The fare_breakdown carries exactly one ERP line, SGD 4.00 for the gantry the trace actually crossed, and the bundle holds no receipt, no second ledger line and no chat message recording any cash payment. There is no duplicate charge for the tribunal to reverse and no billing-integrity finding available under POL-RD-09.
